chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Why the Verne contract ended
summary: Verne's owner wanted a catalog but had no distribution; Machito was released and went to Mercury.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay, you made a lot of recordings with Verne. I believe there are twenty-six recordings that I counted. When did the contract ended with Verne and why?
Ahh - when we finished with them?
Yeah, you were with them in '46, but you weren't with them in '47, so you either finished with them in '46 or the beginning of '47.

Because he says - what-he actually wanted to make a catalog and he didn't have the distribution, he didn't know the business. He thought that just recording was that he was going to make a fortune. But you can have the greatest artists in the world if you not have the connection for distribution, you don't do anything. That even happen with a
big company. You could be a big hit in New York and in Philadelphia they don't know you have recorded with such a company.
Okay, so in 1946 it was all over. Did you part on friendly terms, you know, it was just a business deal?
So there was no problem, right?
Yeah, they give me my release and we went to Mercury.
